rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may stand independently, explain the preceding event, or serve as its بدل اشتمال.
rows.anchor: وجملة { يومئذ تعرضون } مستأنفة ، أو هي بيان لجملة { فيومئذ وقعت الواقعة ، } أو بدل اشتمال منها .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: منكم qualifies خافية but is fronted, making it a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: و { منكم } صفة ل { خافية } قدمت عليه فتكون حالا .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating يومئذ four times magnifies the terror of the day, whose events begin with the trumpet blast.
rows.anchor: وتكرير { يومئذ } أربع مرات لتهويل ذلك اليوم الذي مبدؤه النفخ في الصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is mentioned five times overall: the first يومئذ repeats إذا in the trumpet-blast clause, followed by four repetitions.
rows.anchor: فقد جرى ذكر ذلك اليوم خمس مرات لأن { فيومئذ وقعت الواقعة } تكرير ل ( إذا ) من قوله

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read تخفى with feminine ت; the feminine subject خافية follows a gap and is nonhuman/non-natural feminine.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { لا تخفى } بمثناة فوقية .

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read تخفى with ي because خافية is not naturally feminine and is separated from its verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأه حمزة والكسائي وخلف بالتحتية لأن تأنيث { خافية } غير حقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The presentation is presentation for reckoning and recompense, which introduces the detailed account of people's outcomes.
rows.anchor: الفاء تفصيل لما يتضمنه { تعرضون } ( الحاقة : 18 ) إذ العرض عرض للحساب والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving the book means showing each person the record of their deeds.
rows.anchor: فإيتاء الكتاب هو إيقاف كل واحد على صحيفة أعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أما is both a detailing and conditional particle, conveying مهما يكن من شيء.
rows.anchor: و ( أما ) حرف تفصيل وشرط وهو يفيد مفاد ( مهما يكن من شيء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer's linking فاء is separated from أما by part of its answer to avoid an inelegant direct junction after the condition is elided.
rows.anchor: كرهوا اتصال فاء الجواب بأداة الشرط ففصلوا بينهما بفاصل تحسينا لصورة الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من أوتي كتابه بيمينه is the original opening of the answer, a subject whose predicate is فيقول هاؤم اقرأوا كتابيه.
rows.anchor: فقوله : { من أوتي كتابه بيمينه } أصله صدر جملة الجواب ، وهو مبتدأ خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted clause, “each person is given their book of deeds,” is understood for concision, as in 26:63.
rows.anchor: ودل قوله : { فأما من أوتي كتابه بيمينه } على كلام محذوف للإيجاز تقديره فيؤتى كل أحد كتاب أعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ب in بيمينه expresses accompaniment or means في.
rows.anchor: والباء في قوله : { بيمينه } للمصاحبة أو بمعنى ( في )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the argument from the heavens, Noah turns to the earth and its striking cycle of death and burial, preceded by the creation of people.
rows.anchor: أنشأ الاستدلال بخلق السماوات حضور الأرض في الخيال فأعقب نوح به دليله السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage teaches that humans are formed from earth's elements like plants and embeds the promise of life after death.
rows.anchor: وأدمج في ذلك تعليمهم بأن الإنسان مخلوق من عناصر الأرض مثل النبات وإعلامهم بأن بعد الموت حياة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنبتكم means “created you,” likening human creation to plant growth; the resemblance is especially close because humans are made from earth's elements, as in 3:37 and the idiom “God planted you for good.”
rows.anchor: وأطلق على معنى : أنشأكم ، فعل { أنبتكم } للمشابهة بين إنشاء الإنسان وإنبات النبات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed view takes the implied meaning as “He grew your ancestor,” namely Adam, created from dust in 3:59.
rows.anchor: وقيل التقدير : أنبت أصلكم ، أي آدم عليه السلام ، قال تعالى : { كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نباتا is a verbal noun from أنبت treated as an emphatic direct object, rather than the regular إنباتا.
rows.anchor: و { نباتا } : اسم من أنبت ، عومل معاملة المصدر فوقع مفعولا مطلقا ل { أنبتكم } للتوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lighter, established نباتا is preferred over the heavier إنباتا as a mark of eloquence.
rows.anchor: لأن نباتا أخف فلما تسنى الإتيان به لأنه مستعمل فصيح لم يعدل عنه إلى الثقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إخراجا is kept instead of خروجا because its ending matches the earlier فواصل; preserving such rhyme is a mark of excellence.
rows.anchor: بخلاف قوله بعده { إخراجا } فإنه لم يعدل عنه إلى : خروجا ، لعدم ملاءمته لألفاظ الفواصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection warning is more important than the creation proof, so ثم signals rank rather than time; reburial prepares for the main point, being raised.
rows.anchor: ولكونه أهم رتبة من الاستدلال عليهم بأصل الإنشاء عطفت الجملة ب { ثم } الدالة على التراخي الرتبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic verbal object reinforces the assertion that God will raise them, answering those who deny resurrection.
rows.anchor: وأكد { يخرجكم } بالمفعول المطلق لرد إنكارهم البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura has only the name al-Muzzammil, taken by annexation from its opening; the name may quote the word itself or describe the Prophet's state in 73:1.
rows.anchor: ليس لهذه السورة إلا اسم ( سورة المزمل ) عرفت بالإضافة لهذا اللفظ الواقع في أولها

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the majority considered the sura Makkan except 73:20 to its end; al-Qurtubi attributes the same view to al-Thaʿlabi.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : هي في قول الجمهور مكية إلا قوله تعالى : { إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل

rows.speaker: صاحب الإتقان
rows.claim: The Itqan author cites al-Hakim from ʿAʾisha: the ending was revealed a year after the opening, when night vigil had been imposed before the five prayers, implying the whole sura was Makkan.
rows.anchor: وقال في ( الإتقان ) : إن استثناء قوله : { إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the whole sura is Makkan, the command “Stand at night” in 73:2 was given in Mecca.
rows.anchor: يعني وذلك كله بمكة ، أي فتكون السورة كلها مكية فتعين أن قوله : قم الليل } ( المزمل : 2 ) أمر به في مكة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿAʾisha's report says the ending followed the opening by a year; al-Tabari also reports this timing from Ibn ʿAbbas, while the majority place the ending in Medina years later.
rows.anchor: فقالت عائشة : نزل بعد صدر السورة بسنة ، ومثله روى الطبري عن ابن عباس ، وقال الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers a Medinan date for 73:20 onward because it mentions fighting in God's path, unless this predicts the unseen miraculously.
rows.anchor: فالظاهر أن الأصح أن نزول { إن ربك يعلم إلى آخر السورة نزل بالمدينة لقوله تعالى : وءاخرون يقاتلون في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that the Prophet and a group of companions prayed at night for ten years after 73:1; 73:20 through “establish prayer” then came after ten years, hence in Medina if his Meccan stay lasted ten years.
rows.anchor: وروى الطبري عن سعيد بن جبير ( قال : لما أنزل الله على نبيئه صلى الله عليه وسلم { يا أيها المزمل

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Some of ʿAʾisha's reports imply the entire sura is Makkan and its ending came a year after its opening, before obligatory prayer, as transmitted by al-Hakim via the Itqan author.
rows.anchor: فبعضها يقتضي أن السورة كلها مكية وأن صدرها نزل قبل آخرها بسنة قبل فرض الصلاة وهو ما رواه الحاكم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In another report, people gathered after hearing the Prophet pray; fearing vigil would be prescribed, he left upset. The opening command was treated as obligatory for eight months, then 73:20 lifted it, returning them to the established prayer and removing the extra vigil; al-Tabari transmits it through two lines from Abu Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman from ʿAʾisha.
rows.anchor: وهذا ما رواه الطبري بسندين إلى أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن عائشة ، وهو يقتضي أن السورة كلها مدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That account implies a wholly Medinan sura: ʿAʾisha lived with the Prophet in Medina, and his angry exit suggests he left his home for its adjoining mosque; other reports support mosque prayer.
rows.anchor: ولأن قولها : ( فخرج مغضبا ) يقتضي أنه خرج من بيته المفضي إلى مسجده ، ويؤيده أخبار تثبت قيام الليل في مسجده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inconsistent narratives may have confused the initial imposition of night vigil with later encouragement to perform it.
rows.anchor: ولعل سبب هذا الاضطراب اختلاط في الروايات بين فرض قيام الليل وبين الترغيب فيه

rows.speaker: النخعي
rows.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi, as quoted by al-Qurtubi from al-Thaʿlabi, says the Prophet was wrapped in ʿAʾisha's blanket, half of it on her as she slept and half on him as he prayed; this places the scene in Medina.
rows.anchor: ونسب القرطبي إلى ( تفسير الثعلبي ) قال : قال النخعي في قوله تعالى : { يا أيها المزمل كان النبي متزملا بقطيفة عائشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening certainly came in Mecca, while 73:20 to the end came in Medina years later and abrogated the Prophet's duty; ʿAʾisha's claim that vigil preceded the five prayers is anomalous.
rows.anchor: فالذي نعتمد عليه أن أول السورة نزل بمكة لا محالة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada, with a similar view from al-Dahhak, takes the Prophet's wrapping literally as preparation for prayer before he was told to rise at night.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو تزمل للاستعداد للصلاة فنودي يا أيها المزمل قم الليل إلا قليلا } وهذا مروي عن قتادة . وقريب منه عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima reads “wrapped up” metaphorically as taking on the prophetic mission: expend effort in conveying it by night and day, except necessary sleep.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة : معناه زملت هذا الأمر فقم به ، يريد أمر النبوءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If al-Muzzammil preceded al-Muddaththir, revelation began with 96:1, then answered the accusation of madness prompted by al-Walid, soothed the Prophet after the slander, and later resumed with al-Muddaththir after he saw the angel at Hira.
rows.anchor: فإذا كانت سورة المزمل قد أنزلت قبل سورة المدثر كان ذلك دالا على أن الله تعالى بعد أن ابتدأ رسوله بالوحي بصدر سورة { اقرأ باسم ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muzzammil describes the Prophet's state when addressed; it is not one of his names. Al-Suhayli says it was not known as a name, though some count it among his names.
rows.anchor: فنداء النبي بوصف المزمل } باعتبار حالته وقت ندائه وليس المزمل معدودا من أسماء النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قم is intransitive and means pray, unlike قم in 74:2, which means begin the task of warning.
rows.anchor: وفعل { قم } منزل منزلة اللازم فلا يحتاج إلى تقدير متعلق لأن القيام مراد به الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الليل is an accusative time adverb, the dark period from after ʿisha until dawn; the command covers it except necessary sleep and similar needs.
rows.anchor: و { الليل } : زمن الظلمة من بعد العشاء إلى الفجر . وانتصب { الليل } على الظرفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Qur'anic and Prophetic usage, qiyam al-layl means night prayer apart from Maghrib and ʿIsha and their regular sunnah prayers.
rows.anchor: وقيام الليل لقب في اصطلاح القرآن والسنة للصلاة فيه ما عدا صلاتي المغرب والعشاء ورواتبهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night-prayer command is obligatory for the Prophet alone; Muslims followed his example, and the majority place this before the five daily prayers were prescribed.
rows.anchor: وأمر الرسول بقيام الليل أمر إيجاب وهو خاص به لأن الخطاب موجه إليه وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night prayer purifies the Prophet inwardly and prepares him to receive revelation without the strain described when the angel pressed him before 96:1; 73:5 points to this wisdom.
rows.anchor: هو أن تزداد به سريرته زكاء يقوي استعداده لتلقي الوحي حتى لا يحرجه الوحي

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: A report in al-Bukhari says the angel pressed the Prophet until he was exhausted, then told him to read.
rows.anchor: كما ورد في حديث البخاري : ( فغطني حتى بلغ مني الجهد ) ثم قال : { اقرأ باسم ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God inspired the Prophet to practice tahannuth in Hira before revelation, the author judges that night prayer was obligatory on him before the five prayers, so he was never without worship.
rows.anchor: ولهذا نرجح أن قيام الليل فرض عليه قبل فرض الصلوات الخمس عليه وعلى الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's obligation continued after the five prayers as a special honor: night was free for intimate devotion, and 17:79 calls it an additional nearness for him.
rows.anchor: وقد استمر وجوب قيام الليل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد فرض الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night prayer was never obligatory on the rest of the community; they followed the Prophet, who allowed it, and God praised them for it, as in 32:16.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن واجبا على غيره ولم تفرض على المسلمين صلاة قبل الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿAʾisha says night vigil was imposed at the beginning of the sura, so the Prophet and his companions prayed; there is no disagreement that its obligation was lifted from Muslims, leaving it recommended.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة : ( إن الله افترض قيام الليل في أول هذه السورة فقام النبي وأصحابه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night prayer is established as recommended for Muslims; scholars disagree whether its obligation continued for the Prophet, a question the author says need not be pursued.
rows.anchor: على أنه لا خلاف في رفع فرض القيام عن المسلمين . وتقرر أنه مندوب فيه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains the word metaphorically: night prayer has a stronger beneficial effect and leaves a firmer good and reward in the worshipper.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الوطء مستعارا لحالة صلاة الليل وأثرها في المصلي ، أي أشد أثر خير في نفسه

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmir and Abu ʿAmr alone read وطاء with a kasra, open long vowel, as the verbal noun of واطأ.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر وأبو عمرو وحده { وطاء } بكسر الواو وفتح الطاء ومدها مصدر واطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the variant reading, وطاء means agreement and compatibility, as in 9:37.
rows.anchor: والوطاء : الوفاق والملاءمة ، قال تعالى : { ليواطئوا عدة ما حرم الله }

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says night prayer harmonizes tongue and heart, aligning recited words with their understood meanings because the quiet removes distractions.
rows.anchor: وبحاصل هذا فسر مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هي is a pronoun of separation; here it strengthens the assertion rather than restricting it, and the author cross-refers to its construction in 73:20.
rows.anchor: وضمير { هي } ضمير فصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqwam literally concerns uprightness without crookedness, then is metaphorically used for what is better and more beneficial.
rows.anchor: والأقوم : الأفضل في التقوي الذي هو عدم الاعوجاح والالتواء واستعير { أقوم } للأفضل الأنفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qilan means speech, here Quran recitation in light of the earlier description of revelation as a weighty saying in 73:5.
rows.anchor: و { قيلا } : القول ، وأريد به قراءة القرآن لتقدم قوله : { إنا سنلقي عليك قولا ثقيلا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses “straighter in speech” as making them more likely to understand the Quran.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { وأقوم قيلا } : أدنى من أن يفقهوا القرآن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains it as better preservation of the recitation.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : أحفظ للقراءة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the recitation is straighter because the worshipper is free from worldly affairs.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : أقوم قراءة لفراغه من الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وطأ and قيلا are accusative specification (tamyiz) for أشد and أقوم respectively.
rows.anchor: وانتصب { وطأ } و { قيلا } نسبة تمييزي ل { أشد } ول { أقوم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The uncoordinated sentence does not specify daytime prayers, since the five prayers were not yet prescribed according to the common view.
rows.anchor: فصل هذه الجملة دون عطف على ما قبلها يقتضي أن مضمونها ليس من جنس حكم ما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility is that the day verse explains why night was chosen: its prayer has deeper effect and firmer recitation, while daytime work leaves no solitude for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لأن النهار زمن فيه شغل عظيم لا يترك لك خلوة بنفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse gently justifies the night-prayer burden by allowing daytime rest after fatigue and time for the Prophet's daytime responsibilities.
rows.anchor: وفيه إرشاد إلى أن النهار ظرف واسع لإيقاع ما عسى أن يكلفه فيام الليل من فتور بالنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to remember is coordinated with the night-prayer command, but its unqualified time extends it to night and day, as in 76:25.
rows.anchor: عطف على { قم الليل } ( المزمل : 2 ) وقصد بإطلاق الأمر عن تعيين زمان إلى إفادة تعميمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Name” is included because the commanded remembrance is verbal, while spoken words encompass inward thought since speech follows what is in the mind; compare 7:205.
rows.anchor: وإقحام كلمة { اسم } لأن المأمور به ذكر اللسان وهو جامع للتذكر بالعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabattul is separation: grammatically the reflexive of battala, figuratively intensified as if another caused it; here it means turning thought toward what pleases God, away from people. Imruʾ al-Qays's “منارة ممسى راهب متبتل” illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: والتبتل : شدة البتل ، وهو مصدر تبتل القاصر الذي هو مطاوع بتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabtil is the verbal noun of transitive form battala; using it instead of tabattul signals that separation entails actively cutting oneself off from all but God.
rows.anchor: والتبتيل : مصدر بتل المشدد الذي هو فعل متعد مثل التقطيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired forms portray training the self in detachment, and tabtil also preserves the cadence of the surrounding verse endings.
rows.anchor: فالجمع بين { تبتل } و { تبتيلا } مشير إلى إراضة النفس على ذلك التبتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commanded separation is limited to activities that obstruct night prayer or daytime preaching and disputation; ordinary food, sleep, family, marriage, and perfume can all serve God's religion.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالانقطاع المأمور به انقطاع خاص وهو الانقطاع عن الأعمال التي تمنعه من قيام الليل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that women and perfume had been made beloved to him from worldly things.
rows.anchor: وقد قال : ( حبب إلي من دنياكم النساء والطيب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command does not mean monastic withdrawal from women and managing life, which is incompatible with the Prophet's messenger role.
rows.anchor: وليس هو التبتل المفضي إلى الرهبانية وهو الإعراض عن النساء وعن تدبير أمور الحياة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report in the Sahih, the Prophet rejected ʿUthman ibn Mazʿun's request to withdraw from women; he said that had he permitted it, they would have castrated themselves.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث سعد في ( الصحيح ) ( رد رسول الله على عثمان بن مظعون التبتل ولو أذن له لاختصينا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest devotion is renouncing associationism, the meaning of hanifiyya; this explains the following affirmation that God alone is deity.
rows.anchor: ومن أكبر التبتل إلى الله الانقطاع عن الإشراك ، وهو معنى الحنيفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should continually worship, remain mindful of God, and devote himself to preaching; the command renews his existing practice, guided first through tahannuth at Hira and then revelation.
rows.anchor: وخلاصة المعنى : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مأمور أن لا تخلو أوقاته عن إقبال على عبادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier al-Qalam (68:51) already described the disbelievers nearly tripping the Prophet with their eyes when hearing the Reminder; early suras mostly set duties particular to him.
rows.anchor: فإن في سورة القلم ( وقد نزلت قبل المزمل ) { وإن يكاد الذين كفروا ليزلقونك بأبصارهم لما سمعوا الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Lord of east and west suits remembrance across night and day, which begin at sunset and sunrise and each extends until its opposite.
rows.anchor: ووصف الله بأنه { رب المشرق والمغرب } لمناسبة الأمر بذكره في الليل وذكره في النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean the directions east and west, encompassing all earthly directions and thus the whole world, or the times of sunrise and sunset, the endpoints of night and day.
rows.anchor: فيصح أن يكون المشرق والمغرب جهتي الشروق والغروب ، فيكون لاستيعاب جهات الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عرفة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿArafa reports some teachers' view that a person may choose which path to identify; he calls this good and says the verse's apparent sense remains.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير ابن عرفة الذي كان بعض شيوخنا يحملها على أنه مخير في تعيين السبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says his prior explanation removes the need for Ibn ʿArafa's construction: the verse contains no notion of choice.
rows.anchor: وقد علمت مما قررناه أنه لا حاجة إليه وأن ليس في الآية شيء بمعنى التخيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “To his Lord” depicts the seeker of success and guidance as a traveler shown a path to a generous protector, with no remaining obstacle to walking it.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : { إلى ربه } تمثيل لحال طالب الفوز والهدى بحال السائر إلى ناصر أو كريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion from this point concerns the portion of the sura revealed in Medina, as stated in the introduction.
rows.anchor: من هنا يبتدىء ما نزل من هذه السورة بالمدينة كما تقدم ذكره في أول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows the Prophet and some companions already prayed at night under the opening command; its “He relented toward you” marks relief for all and abrogates that earlier command.
rows.anchor: وصريح هذه الآية ينادي على أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقوم من الليل قبل نزول الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Early authorities differed over when and where this verse was revealed and how its ruling relates to the preceding verse; the trusted view is that the opening was Makkan.
rows.anchor: واختلف السلف في وقت نزولها ومكانه وفي نسبة مقتضاها من مقتضى الآية التي قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Tabari's report from Abu Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman from ʿAʾisha, and the similar report from al-Nakhaʿi about the blanket, as evidence that the opening was Medinan.
rows.anchor: ولا يغتر بما رواه الطبري عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن عائشة مما يوهم أن صدر السورة نزل بالمدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first command obligated night prayer for the Prophet alone; companions in Mecca followed his example. ʿAʾisha thought the five prayers abrogated a duty on Muslims, but the author calls that an interpretation.
rows.anchor: في أن القيام الذي شرع في صدر السورة كان قياما واجبا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first obligation on the community was the five prayers imposed on the Night Journey; if an earlier communal prayer existed, the Miʿraj account would mention its replacement, and the five were equally obligatory on the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ولو كان لجرى ذكر تعويضه بالصلوات الخمس في حديث المعراج

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says only 73:20 abrogated the night vigil.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس لأنه قال : إن قيام الليل لم ينسخه إلا آية : { إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five prayers did not abrogate the Prophet's night vigil; rather, “recite what is easy” removed the requirement to spend half the night or slightly less.
rows.anchor: ولا أن يختلف في أن فرض الصلوات الخمس لم ينسخ فرض القيام على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سوى أنه نسخ استيعاب نصف الليل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas recounts staying with his aunt Maymuna: the Prophet awoke around midnight, performed ablutions, prayed thirteen rakʿas, then slept until the dawn caller; Ibn ʿAbbas was a boy, dating it to about 7 or 8 AH.
rows.anchor: وقد بين ذلك حديث ابن عباس ليلة بات في بيت خالته ميمونة أم المؤمنين قال فيه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The only reported group prayer with the Prophet occurred in Medina during Ramadan after he reserved mosque space; companions joined, then he stayed away one night, saying he feared it might be made obligatory.
rows.anchor: إلا حين احتجز موضعا من المسجد لقيامه في ليالي رمضان فتسامع أصحابه به فجعلوا ينسلون إلى المسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This shows the companions' joint night prayer was not obligatory and did not continue; if any vigil were mandatory for Muslims, praying with the Prophet would fulfill it and there would be no fear of a new duty.
rows.anchor: وهو صريح في أن القيام الذي قاموه مع الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يكن فرضا عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet told Hafsa that ʿAbd Allah was righteous and would be better if he prayed at night.
rows.anchor: وقد عضد ذلك حديث ابن عمر ( أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لحفصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening praises the Prophet's faithful, earnest fulfillment of the command: he regularly prayed the prescribed half night or slightly less, and went as far as nearly two-thirds.
rows.anchor: وافتتاح الكلام ب { إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم } يشعر بالثناء عليه لوفائه بحق القيام الذي أمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His near-two-thirds vigil represents the utmost limit, as with resolute messengers; the Prophet compared Moses's completion of the term to choosing the longer ten-year period in 28:29.
rows.anchor: بل أخذ بالأقصى وذلك ما يقرب من ثلثي الليل كما هو شأن أولي العزم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says the Prophet prayed at night until his feet swelled.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء في الحديث : ( أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقوم من الليل حتى تورمت قدماه )
